newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GIANTS WIN FIRST EVER INTERLEAGUE GAME.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GIANTS WIN FIRST EVER INTERLEAGUE GAME.

text.p: Stan Javier was the hero of baseball's first regular-season interleague game as the National League's San Francisco Giants edged the American League's Texas Rangers 4-3 at the Ballpark in Arlington.
In three later games on the first night of interleague play in the major leagues, the homestanding American League clubs came out victorious.
Javier hit the first home run in the history of interleague play and drove in the winning run with an RBI double in the seventh inning to lead Giants to victory.
Despite the loss by the home team, Giants manager Dusty Baker noted: "The fans were really into it."

Mark Gardner (7-2) pitched eight innings and allowed two earned runs and eight hits to get the win. Rod Beck retired three batters on just four pitches in the ninth for his 20th save, tying him with Baltimore's Randy Myers and Mariano Rivera of the Yankees for the major league lead in saves.
All results and statistics of interleague play will count for the teams involved.
"It was very exciting," said Gardner, who admitted he had not considered the historical significance of the game. "I'm sure down the road I'll think about it."

The Giants rallied for three runs off Texas starter Darren Oliver (3-8) in the seventh to erase a 3-1 deficit, capped by Javier's double to the right field corner that scored Barry Bonds with the winning run.

The legions of baseball history buffs will note: The first batter in interleague history was Giants centerfielder Darryl Hamilton, who lined a single to right field off Oliver on the third pitch of the game for the first interleague hit.

Texas' Bill Ripken, who had two hits and two RBI, drove in Damon Buford with the first run of interleague play. Javier then hit the first interleague home run in the third inning to tie the game at 1-1.
In Oakland, Patrick Lennon's pinch-hit two-run single off Mark Guthrie highlighted a four-run sixth inning as the AL Oakland Athletics edged the NL Los Angeles Dodger 5-4.

Dodgers starter Hideo Nomo (6-6), who does not usually issue many walks, loaded the bases on two walks and a hit batter in the sixth, then walked Jose Canseco to force in a run as Oakland tied the game 2-2.
Nomo was replaced by Guthrie. But Lennon delivered a two-run single to shallow right and George Williams followed with an RBI double to give the A's a 5-2 lead.
Dave Telgheder (2-3) allowed four runs and eight hits over 6 1/3 innings for the win. Nomo gave up only one hit in his 5 1/3 innings, but walked five to suffer the loss.
In Anaheim, Tony Phillips homered and drove in two runs and Jim Edmonds's RBI single snapped a seventh-inning tie as the AL Angels beat the NL San Diego Padres 8-4.
With two out in the sixth, Phillips hit an 0-1 pitch from Heath Murray (1-1) over the left-field fence to give the Angels a 4-3 lead.
The Padres tied the score in the seventh, but the Angels took the lead for good in the bottom of the inning when Edmonds delivered an RBI single and later scored on Gary DiSarcina's sacrifice fly.
Dave Hollins and Darin Erstad also homered for the Angels. John Flaherty and Rickey Henderson homered for San Diego.
In Seattle, Jay Buhner's three-run double capped a four-run seventh inning as the AL Mariners overcame a six-run deficit for a wild 12-11 victory over the NL Colorado Rockies.
The teams combined for 23 runs and 30 hits -- 12 for Seattle and 18 for Colorado -- despite no home runs from either club.

Vinny Castilla and Quinton McCracken each had three hits and three RBI and Andres Galarraga was 4-for-5 with an RBI and two runs scored for Colorado. Ken Griffey and Buhner each drove in three runs for Seattle.
Bob Wells (2-0), the fourth of six Seattle pitchers, got the win. Mike Munoz (1-1), the fourth Colorado pitcher, suffered the loss.
